interface.title: Colony Detection and Identification (AgarVision colony counter)
interface.stage_of_work: Analysing plate images after incubation: counting and classifying colonies
interface.what_it_is_for: Upload photos of agar plates and have YOLOv8 models count the colonies or sort them by bacterial species, using a confidence threshold you can change and boxes drawn on each image.

data.note: I uploaded the two provided test files, colonies_plate.jpg (dark blobs on grey) and blank_plate.jpg (plain grey). They are tiny synthetic images, so the results only show how the interface behaves, not real accuracy. The README already warns that the model is poor. Each run took several seconds; the 'Running…' indicator showed while it worked.

features.name: Switch from counting to per-class counts with a colour legend
features.general: Switch the same images from a counting model to a classifying model. The output changes from one total per image to a list of each class found, with its count and a colour swatch meant to match that class's boxes on the image. Anyone reusing this pattern should draw the legend and the overlay in the same colour order; this tool does not.
features.specific: 'Choose Mode' radio: Count gives 'Detected Colonies: N'; Identify gives 'Detected Species' with lines like 'Staphylococcus aureus: 237' and a coloured swatch under each plate. Confirmed defect: boxes are drawn on the BGR image with the colour triple, the image is then converted to RGB, and the swatch uses the triple as RGB (Streamlit-UI.py lines 61-68 and 97), so any colour whose red and blue differ shows a swatch that does not match its boxes (screens/028.webp: purple and lime swatches beside magenta and teal boxes; screens/032.webp: orange-red swatch beside a blue box). Magenta, where red and blue are equal, matches (screens/030.webp). Colours are picked at random on every run.
steps: upload plates and choose Count to read one total per plate
choose Identify: the caption becomes 'Detected Species' with a per-species list
set the threshold low enough for detections to appear (none at 0.10; 7 species at 0.00)
compare swatch colours with the boxes, expecting mismatches except where red equals blue
serves_tasks: Choose whether to count or classify

screens_never_reached: A larger view of the result image: Fullscreen (screens/014.webp) shows it at its native size of about 130 px, so individual boxes are hard to tell apart
Deploy, Print and Record screen in the main menu: these come with Streamlit, are not part of this tool, and I did not open them
not_done: Checking that counts are accurate against real colonies: the test files are tiny synthetic images, and the README warns the model is inaccurate

Confirming that Identify mode gives identical species counts at a given threshold every time: at 0.03 it first showed three species in screens/027.webp, captured while the run was still in progress, then two in screens/028.webp. Counts were unchanged on Rerun (screens/032.webp), and the replay saw the same in Count mode at 0.10 and Identify mode at 0.00. Box and legend colours are reassigned at random on every run.

Confirmed defect, not a one-off: legend swatches do not match box colours. Boxes are drawn in BGR and the swatch uses the same triple as RGB (Streamlit-UI.py lines 61-68 and 97), so every colour whose red and blue differ is shown wrongly in the legend: screens/028.webp (purple and lime swatches, magenta and teal boxes) and screens/032.webp (orange-red swatch, blue box). Magenta matched (screens/030.webp) because its red and blue are equal.
The negative-control check only partly passes: blank_plate reads 0 at 0.10 and 0.30, but 300 colonies at 0.00 (screens/036.webp) and six spurious species in Identify mode at 0.00 (screens/026.webp)
Exporting or recording results: the interface has no download or export control, so per-plate counts for a batch or replicate comparison must be copied down by hand; this was not done
Uploading real photos or PNG files: only the two provided test files were available
Training or validating a model on your own plates: the README lists command-line scripts (scripts/train.py, validate.py) for this, which are outside the interface and not covered here
